summary: The FRONTIER Act establishes Federal oversight for the development and deployment of frontier artificial intelligence models in interstate and foreign commerce. The bill creates definitions and requirements for large and very large frontier AI developers, institutes an independent verification organization (IVO) licensing framework, mandates reporting of critical safety incidents and catastrophic risks, provides the Secretary of Commerce with emergency order authority for imminent risks, and preempts certain state laws related to AI risk transparency, third-party auditing, and incident reporting.

affected_groups.effect: Must comply with federal oversight, maintain and publish frontier AI frameworks, undergo third-party audits and independent verification assessments, register and pay fees, report safety incidents, and face civil or criminal penalties for noncompliance.
affected_groups.group: Large and Very Large Frontier AI Developers

affected_groups.effect: Must obtain a license from the Under Secretary of Commerce, meet conflict-of-interest and funding-transparency requirements, perform assessments on very large developers, submit reports, and receive limited immunity from suit.

The Under Secretary of Commerce for AI Security and the Secretary of Commerce are tasked with rulemaking, licensing IVOs, reviewing safety reports, submitting annual reports to Congress, and issuing emergency orders.
affected_groups.group: Department of Commerce and Federal Government

key_provisions: Establishes the position of Under Secretary of Commerce for AI Security and requires the issuance of minimum requirements for frontier AI frameworks within 180 days.

Requires large frontier developers to publish frontier AI frameworks, undergo annual compliance audits, submit transparency reports before deployment, file registration disclosures, and report critical safety incidents and catastrophic risks.
Establishes a licensing and oversight regime for independent verification organizations (IVOs) to assess very large frontier developers and provides IVOs with limited legal immunity.

Grants the Secretary of Commerce the authority to issue provisional and final emergency orders to suspend or restrict the development, deployment, or internal use of a frontier model presenting an imminent catastrophic risk.

Preempts state and local laws and regulations that impose new substantive obligations on artificial intelligence developers regarding frontier AI risk transparency, third-party auditing, and incident reporting.
missing_information: Specific dollar amounts for registration and licensing fees charged to large frontier developers and IVOs are not defined in the source text.
The exact technical compute threshold operations number is formatted as 10-26 in the text, but specific operational budget impacts or exact numbers of affected companies are not provided.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The FRONTIER Act establishes Federal oversight for the development and deployment of frontier artificial intelligence models in interstate and foreign commerce. The bill creates definitions and requirements for large and very large frontier AI developers, institutes an independent verification organization (IVO) licensing framework, mandates reporting of critical safety incidents and catastrophic risks, provides the Secretary of Commerce with emergency order authority for imminent risks, and preempts certain state laws related to AI risk transparency, third-party auditing, and incident reporting.
summary_detail.significance: The bill creates a comprehensive federal regulatory and oversight framework specifically targeting the development and deployment of the most powerful artificial intelligence models, potentially shifting oversight authority from state jurisdictions to the federal government.
